Min-max likelihood penalty

min_max_likelihood.Rd

Penalises model predictions that fall outside the [obs_lower, obs_upper] envelope defined in the observed data. Predictions within the envelope incur no penalty; predictions below the lower bound or above the upper bound are penalised proportionally to how far they deviate, scaled by 1e6 to dominate the objective function.

Usage

min_max_likelihood(obs, sim)

Arguments

obs

Numeric matrix with two columns: column 1 is the lower bound (obs_lower) and column 2 is the upper bound (obs_upper) of the observed data envelope. One row per time step or observation.

sim

Numeric vector of simulated values, one entry per row of obs.

Value

A non-negative scalar. Returns 0 when all simulated values lie within their respective [obs_lower, obs_upper] bounds, and a large positive value otherwise (intended to be minimised as part of the calibration objective function).

Details

The penalty is computed as a log-ratio: $$-10^6 \sum \min\!\left(\log\frac{s+1}{l+1}, 0\right) + 10^6 \sum \max\!\left(\log\frac{s+1}{u+1}, 0\right)$$ where \(s\) is the simulated value, \(l\) the lower bound, and \(u\) the upper bound. Adding 1 to numerator and denominator avoids division by zero when values are near zero.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  obs <- cbind(lower = c(10, 20, 30), upper = c(15, 25, 35))
  sim <- c(12, 18, 40)   # 18 below lower[2], 40 above upper[3]
  min_max_likelihood(obs, sim)
} # }
